results.reason: Issue 1 explains the automatic five-year Renewal Terms and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calls this a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for another five years.

Issue 4 identifies exclusivity covering all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass beer bottles at U.S./Canadian facilities. It states Harrowgate is now contractually barred under the executed text.
Issue 2 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 and that the objection deadline was September 2, 2026. It says the increase is deemed accepted, with the amendment dated September 21, 2026.

Issue 3 explains that Amendment §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It says recall and personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

The memo identifies new §14.4 allowing assignment to Affiliates and successors without consent, and mentions a competitor's affiliate as a risk. It does not explain that Harrowgate remains bound by the §14.3 consent requirement, so it never addresses the one-sided nature of the restriction.
The memo never mentions Section 15.2 or the order of precedence by which the amendment controls over the Supply Agreement.
Issue 3 states the §11.1 cap equals the fees paid in the six months before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to [Partner] and lists issues item by item. Each item has a 'Where' location and a 'Recommended fix'.
It proposes specific language for a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1, a revised §2.2 renewal clause and §14.4, among others.
It treats the increase as deemed accepted and binding. It does not suggest the objection window remains open.
It treats §3.1 as binding and recommends amending it. It does not conclude that the term sheet governs.
